title: Continuous conormal lift maps preserve differential augmentations
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $S$ a finite-type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], $\mathfrak m$ a maximal ideal with residue field $k$, $A=S_{\mathfrak m}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and $R=\widehat A$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Put $M_R=\Omega^1_{A/k}\otimes_A R$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials, def-weil-module-base-change], and let $\widehat d:R\to M_R$ be the continuous extension of the universal derivation [def-trf-completed-differential-extension]. Let $A=P/I$ with $P=k[u_1,\ldots,u_m]_{\mathfrak q}$ at a $k$-rational maximal ideal, and let $\pi:T=k[[z_1,\ldots,z_n]]\twoheadrightarrow R$ be a continuous local $k$-algebra surjection with kernel $J$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Set
$$C_P=[I/I^2\xrightarrow{\mathrm d}\Omega^1_{P/k}\otimes_P A],\qquad C_T=[J/J^2\xrightarrow{\widehat{\mathrm d}}R^n]$$
in degrees $-1,0$, using termwise formal partial derivatives for the second differential. A local $k$-algebra lift $\alpha:P\to T$ of $P\to A\to R$ exists. Every such lift gives a well-defined chain map $f_\alpha:C_P\otimes_A R\to C_T$ with
$$[h]\otimes1\mapsto[\alpha(h)],\qquad \mathrm du_i\otimes1\mapsto\widehat{\mathrm d}\alpha(u_i).$$
For every $h\in T$ one has the continuous chain rule
$$\widehat d(\pi(h))=\sum_i\pi(\partial h/\partial z_i)\,\widehat d(\pi(z_i)).$$
Consequently $q_T f_\alpha=q_P$, where the augmentations send $\mathrm du_i$ to $\mathrm d\bar u_i\otimes1$ and $e_i$ to $\widehat d(\pi(z_i))$. If $\pi':T'=k[[w_1,\ldots,w_{n'}]]\twoheadrightarrow R$ is another such presentation with kernel $J'$ and $\beta:T\to T'$ is a continuous local $k$-algebra map with $\pi'\beta=\pi$, then $[g]\mapsto[\beta(g)]$ and $e_i\mapsto\widehat{\mathrm d}\beta(z_i)$ give a chain map $h_\beta:C_T\to C_{T'}$ satisfying $q_{T'}h_\beta=q_T$. These formulas respect identities and composition of the presentation maps. The corresponding algebraic conormal maps for local maps between polynomial-local presentations of $A$ likewise commute with their augmentations, also after extension to $R$.

proof.text: Write $\mathfrak a=(z_1,\ldots,z_n)$ and $a_i=u_i\bmod\mathfrak q\in k$. Choose $v_i\in T$ with $\pi(v_i)=\bar u_i\in R$. The residue map of the local surjection $\pi$ identifies $T/\mathfrak a=k$ with the residue field of $R$, so $v_i(0)=a_i$. Evaluation $u_i\mapsto v_i$ defines a map $k[u]\to T$. For $s\notin\mathfrak q$ its image has constant coefficient $s(a_1,\ldots,a_m)\ne0$, hence is a unit by the power-series local-ring lemma. Thus $p/s\mapsto p(v)s(v)^{-1}$ is well defined on $P$: equality of fractions is preserved after multiplying by the unit image of a common denominator. It defines $\alpha:P\to T$ lifting the given map to $R$. Its inverse image of $\mathfrak a$ is $\mathfrak qP$, by the same residue calculation, so it is local. In particular $\alpha(I)\subset J$.

source.place: Localization fractions, Tag 00CO (definition-localization); power-series local-ring lemma, applied over the field k. Agent coordinate-lift construction accompanying Varieties Tag 0C52.

proof.text: The polynomial differential basis and localization isomorphism identify $\Omega_{P/k}$ with $\bigoplus_iP\,\mathrm du_i$. Let $D_T:T\to T^n$ have coordinates the formal partial derivatives; it is a $k$-derivation by their defining Leibniz laws. The universal property of $\Omega_{P/k}$ applied to $D_T\alpha$, then reduction modulo $J$, gives an $R$-linear map $f^0_\alpha:(\Omega_{P/k}\otimes_PA)\otimes_AR\to R^n$ with $f^0_\alpha(\mathrm dp\otimes1)=D_T\alpha(p)\bmod J$ for every $p\in P$. In particular its values on $\mathrm du_i$ are precisely the asserted gradients. The assignment $[h]\mapsto[\alpha(h)]$ sends $I/I^2$ to $J/J^2$: $\alpha(I^2)\subset J^2$, and $[\alpha(ph)]=\bar p[\alpha(h)]$, where $\bar p$ acts through $A\to R$. Tensoring this $A$-linear assignment with $R$ gives $f^{-1}_\alpha$.

source.place: Tags 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring), 00RT (lemma-differentials-localize), 00RO (lemma-universal-omega): derivation-induced maps and reduction of ideal classes.

proof.text: The differentials of the conormal complexes are well defined: for $h,h'\in I$, $\mathrm d(hh')=h\,\mathrm dh'+h'\,\mathrm dh$ vanishes after tensoring with $A$, and for $g,g'\in J$, $D_T(gg')=gD_Tg'+g'D_Tg$ vanishes modulo $J$. For $h\in I$ the defining equality from Step 2 reads $f^0_\alpha(\mathrm dh\otimes1)=D_T\alpha(h)\bmod J=d_{C_T}f^{-1}_\alpha([h]\otimes1)$. The ideal classes and their scalar multiples generate the degree $-1$ term, so this proves the chain-map equation. The universal differential $A\to\Omega_{A/k}$ likewise defines $q_P$ on degree zero, with $q_P(\mathrm dh)=0$ for $h\in I$.

source.place: Tag 00RU (lemma-differential-seq), proof: Leibniz kills squares and relation differentials. Explicit application to the two displayed complexes.

proof.text:
Apply the completion--differential comparison with residue extension $F=k$ and its structural section. The derivation $\widehat d$ of the statement satisfies both clauses of [def-trf-completed-differential-extension], so by the uniqueness in clause (i) of the comparison it is the continuous extension used there. Its isomorphism $\eta:M_R\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_r\Omega_{(R/\mathfrak m_R^r)/k}$ sends $\widehat d(x)$ to $(\mathrm d(x\bmod\mathfrak m_R^r))_r$. Here $\mathfrak m_R$ is the maximal ideal of $R$. For each $r\ge1$, locality of $\pi$ gives $T/\mathfrak a^r\to R/\mathfrak m_R^r$. The universal property of differentials gives a map on their differential modules sending $\mathrm d\bar h$ to $\mathrm d\overline{\pi(h)}$. Apply this map to the finite-level gradient identity in the adic-gradient-control lemma. The result is
$$\mathrm d(\pi(h)\bmod\mathfrak m_R^r)=\sum_i(\pi(\partial_i h)\bmod\mathfrak m_R^r)\,\mathrm d(\pi(z_i)\bmod\mathfrak m_R^r).$$
This holds for every $r$; equality of compatible sequences and injectivity of $\eta$ give exactly the asserted chain rule in $M_R$. For $h\in J$ its left side is zero, hence the map $e_i\mapsto\widehat d(\pi(z_i))$ kills the conormal differential and defines the augmentation $q_T$.

source.place: Tag 0C4D (lemma-nodal), completed Jacobian comparison; Algebra Tag 02HQ (lemma-differential-mod-power-ideal) and Tag 00RX, via the cited finite-level gradient theorem. Agent assembly of these existing auxiliary statements.

proof.text:
For every basis differential of $C_P^0\otimes_AR$, Step 4 with $h=\alpha(u_i)$ gives
$$q_Tf^0_\alpha(\mathrm du_i\otimes1)=\widehat d(\pi\alpha(u_i))=\mathrm d\bar u_i\otimes1=q_P(\mathrm du_i\otimes1).$$
The middle equality is $\pi\alpha(u_i)=\bar u_i$ and the extension clause (i) of [def-trf-completed-differential-extension].
Thus the augmentations agree on all degree-zero elements by the basis of Step 2. Both have zero degree $-1$ component, so $q_Tf_\alpha=q_P$ as maps to $M_R[0]$. No smoothness, reducedness, or regular-sequence hypothesis has been used.

source.place: Tags 00RX and 00RT: evaluation on the basis already established in Step 2; the chain rule established in Step 4.

proof.text:
For a formal presentation map $\beta:T\to T'$, $\beta(J)\subset J'$ and $\beta(J^2)\subset J'^2$, so its ideal-class map is well defined and $R$-linear. For each $j$, $E_j=\partial'_j\circ\beta$ is a $k$-linear $\beta$-derivation $T\to T'$. Locality gives $\beta(\mathfrak a)\subset(w_1,\ldots,w_{n'})$, so the relative-derivation expansion applies and gives
$$\partial'_j\beta(g)=\sum_i\beta(\partial_i g)\,\partial'_j\beta(z_i).$$
Reduce this equality modulo $J'$. Since $\pi'\beta=\pi$, it is exactly $d_{C_{T'}}h^{-1}_\beta([g])=h^0_\beta d_{C_T}([g])$, proving the chain condition for the stated degree-zero map. Repeating Step 4 for $\pi'$ gives
$$q_{T'}h^0_\beta(e_i)=\sum_j\pi'(\partial'_j\beta(z_i))\widehat d(\pi'(w_j))=\widehat d(\pi'\beta(z_i))=q_T(e_i).$$
Therefore $q_{T'}h_\beta=q_T$.

source.place: Tag 0C4B (lemma-fitting-ideal-well-defined), chain-rule paragraph, with the full relative-derivation expansion supplied by the cited node. Augmentation equality uses the already proved Step 4 for the second presentation.

proof.text: Identities act as identities on ideal classes, while $\partial_jz_i=\delta_{ij}$ makes their degree-zero matrices identity matrices. For composable formal presentation maps $\beta:T\to T'$ and $\gamma:T'\to T''$, the degree $-1$ composite sends $[g]$ to $[\gamma\beta(g)]$. On $e_i$ the $l$th coordinate of the degree-zero composite is $\sum_j\pi''\gamma(\partial'_j\beta(z_i))\,\pi''(\partial''_l\gamma(w_j))$. The relative-derivation expansion for $\gamma$, evaluated at $\beta(z_i)$, identifies it with $\pi''(\partial''_l\gamma\beta(z_i))$, the coordinate of $h_{\gamma\beta}$. The same calculation at $\alpha(u_i)$ proves $h_\beta f_\alpha=f_{\beta\alpha}$; the degree $-1$ equality is again evaluation on ideal classes. Thus the displayed maps respect identities and composition, including the polynomial-to-formal maps.

source.place: Tag 0C4B (lemma-fitting-ideal-well-defined): explicit chain-rule matrix multiplication, using the relative-derivation expansion cited in Step 6.

proof.text: Finally let $\rho:P\to P'$ be a local $k$-algebra map between localized polynomial presentations of $A$, inducing its identity. The universal property gives $\mathrm dp\mapsto\mathrm d\rho(p)$, and $[h]\mapsto[\rho(h)]$ gives the conormal map. The ideal-square and chain equations are the Leibniz calculation of Step 3. Fractions cause no additional assertion: $0=D(ss^{-1})$ gives $D(s^{-1})=-s^{-2}D(s)$, hence $D(p/s)=s^{-1}D(p)-ps^{-2}D(s)$ for each of the derivations involved. On every $\mathrm dp$, the two augmentation composites equal $\mathrm d\bar p$, since $\rho$ induces the identity of $A$. These symbols generate $\Omega_{P/k}$ by its definition, so the maps agree. Tensoring the equality with $R$ proves the completed assertion. Identities and composition follow on the same ideal classes and symbols $\mathrm dp$; a polynomial presentation change followed by a formal lift gives $f_{\alpha'\rho}$ because both degree-zero maps take $\mathrm dp$ to $D_T\alpha'\rho(p)\bmod J$.
